table.title: [val] العربية / עברית · Bidi with numbers
table.md:
| الرمز | المدينة | עיר | السكان | ملاحظات |
|---|---|---|--:|---|
| RUH | الرياض | ריאד | 7,676,654 | عاصمة المملكة العربية السعودية وأكبر مدنها من حيث عدد السكان. |
| JED | جدة | ג'דה | 3,751,722 | ميناء رئيسي على البحر الأحمر |
| TLV | تل أبيب | תל אביב | 474,530 | מרכז כלכלי ותרבותי, ידועה בחופים ובחיי הלילה שלה. |

understanding.purpose: يعرض الجدول مدناً بأسمائها العربية والعبرية، مع رموزها وأعداد سكانها وملاحظات وصفية عنها.
understanding.reading: يُقرأ الصف من اليمين إلى اليسار كوحدة واحدة؛ تساعد الرموز والأسماء على تحديد المدينة، ثم تُقارن أعداد السكان وتُقرأ الملاحظات للتفاصيل.
groups: العمودان 2 و3 يقدمان اسمي المدينة بالعربية والعبرية، ويجب أن يبقيا متجاورين وسهلَي المطابقة.
العمود 1 يحدد المدينة برمز قصير، والعمود 4 يقدم قيمة رقمية قابلة للمقارنة، والعمود 5 يقدم وصفاً مكملاً.
keep_intact: الكلمات المنفردة في أسماء المدن والملاحظات.
may_wrap: يمكن أن تلتف الملاحظات الطويلة طبيعياً بين الكلمات، فتزيد ارتفاع الصف.
يمكن أن يلتف الاسم العبري المكوّن من أكثر من كلمة؛ وقد تستوعب الأسطر المطلوبة للملاحظات هذا الالتفاف دون زيادة إضافية في ارتفاع الصف.

preferred.name: r0A
preferred.note: يحافظ على أسماء المدن والقيم الرقمية في سطر واحد ويترك الملاحظات للالتفاف.

preferred.name: r1B
preferred.note: Keep this as the alternative when single-line city names matter more than row height. It is identical to r0A because the stated minimum widths leave no room to widen the notes while keeping the longest Hebrew name intact.

preferred.name: r3A
preferred.note: Give the Hebrew name column the 79px needed to keep תל אביב on one line, taking 10px from the notes column. This makes paired names easier to scan; the render should confirm whether the narrower notes increase row heights.

acceptable.name: r0B
acceptable.note: يمنح الملاحظات أكبر عرض ممكن مع السماح للأسماء العبرية متعددة الكلمات بالالتفاف.

acceptable.name: r0C
acceptable.note: يوازن بين مساحة الملاحظات ومساحة الأسماء العبرية، مستفيداً من ارتفاع صفوف الملاحظات عند الحاجة إلى التفاف الاسم.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Split the difference between r0B and r0C: give the Hebrew names a little more room while retaining 181px for notes. The two-word Hebrew name may wrap, but the notes should still have room for a three-line maximum.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: تخصيص الحد اللازم لأطول كلمة عبرية كاملة ومنح 7px إضافية للملاحظات؛ يختبر تخفيف التفاف الوصف مع قبول التفاف الاسم العبري بين كلماته.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: منح العمود العبري 7px إضافية مقارنةً بـr1A مع إبقاء مساحة الملاحظات أكبر منها في r1B؛ يختبر حلاً وسطاً بين راحة قراءة الأسماء وطول الصفوف.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: The population column has only 59px of text space, less than the 76px needed by its longest value. A number would have to break or overflow, making comparisons harder.
bad.why: The population column has only 59px of text space, less than the 76px needed by its longest value. A number would have to break or overflow, making comparisons harder.

rationale: The preferred designs keep both Arabic and Hebrew city names on one line, making each row easy to identify and compare across languages. The notes column is narrower, so the first note takes four lines, but the prose wraps at word boundaries and remains readable. The three preferred candidates have identical widths and render identically.

general: Protect the readability of identifiers and comparison values when distributing width.
Judge wrapping in relation to the role of the content: prose can often wrap more comfortably than a short label or a number.
Use the rendered table to assess row rhythm and the relationship between columns, not just its total height.
specific: A 79px Hebrew city column keeps the two-word city name together; the narrower candidates wrap it.
Keeping that city name intact leaves 164px for notes within the width limit, producing a four-line first note.

tradeoffs: The acceptable designs use a narrower Hebrew city column to give the notes more room, reducing the first data row by one line. A designer could reasonably prefer the shorter table over keeping the Hebrew city name on one line.
uncertain: The ranges are conservative: at the available width, the stated minimums for the first four columns leave exactly 164px for notes. Small coordinated adjustments might look equally good, but the supplied renders do not establish their limits.

critique.good: All city names, codes and population figures stay on one line. The Arabic and Hebrew names are easy to match across each row.
critique.problems: The first note occupies four lines, making its row noticeably taller than the others. The notes feel cramped despite their importance as descriptive text.
critique.cause: The Hebrew-name column is 79px wide, enough for its longest name on one line, but that leaves only 164px for notes.

critique.good: The 188px notes column reduces the first note to three lines. The rows are more balanced, and codes, population figures and individual words remain intact.
critique.problems: The Hebrew name for Tel Aviv wraps onto two lines. Its narrow column looks compressed beside the Arabic-name column, although the wrap does not increase the row height.
critique.cause: At 55px, the Hebrew-name column has only 34px of text space, just enough for its longest individual word but not the complete two-word name.

critique.good: The notes retain the three-line maximum, and the wider Hebrew-name column gives the paired city names a more comfortable visual relationship. All individual words and numbers remain intact.
critique.problems: The Hebrew name for Tel Aviv still wraps, so the additional width does not restore all names to one line. The notes column is narrower than in r0B without reducing the table's height.
critique.cause: The 68px Hebrew-name column provides 47px of text space, below the 58px needed for the full name; its extra 13px comes from the notes column.

critique.good: يحافظ على الرموز وأعداد السكان والكلمات كاملة، وتبقى أسماء المدن العربية والعبرية متجاورة. عرض الملاحظات يسمح بقراءة الوصف في ثلاثة أسطر كحد أقصى، مع صفوف متوازنة نسبياً.
critique.problems: ينقسم الاسم العبري تل أبيب إلى سطرين، فيصعب مسحه مقابل الاسم العربي قليلاً، وإن كان ارتفاع صفه يستوعب ذلك دون زيادة. عمودا الأسماء ضيقان بصرياً مقارنة بالملاحظات.
critique.cause: عرض العمود 3 هو 62px، ولا يترك سوى 41px للنص، أقل من 58px اللازمة لاسم תל אביב في سطر واحد.

critique.good: تبقى أسماء المدن العبرية كاملة في سطر واحد، مما يسهل مطابقتها مع الأسماء العربية، وتحافظ بقية الأعمدة على الرموز والأرقام كاملة.
critique.problems: تلتف ملاحظة الرياض إلى أربعة أسطر، فيطول صفها ويصبح توزيع النص أثقل وأقل توازناً. لا يقابل التحسن في عمود الأسماء العبري فائدة تكفي لتعويض تقلص مساحة الملاحظات.
critique.cause: زيادة عرض العمود 3 إلى 79px أخذت 17px من العمود 5، فأصبح عرضه 164px ومساحة نصه 143px.

critique.good: The table fits the viewport, all headers stay on one line, and codes and population figures remain intact. The wider notes column gives the descriptions a reasonably even rhythm, while each row remains easy to follow across the two city-name columns.
critique.problems: The Hebrew name תל אביב wraps, making the third row’s paired city names less immediately comparable. The notes still need three lines in the first and last data rows.
critique.cause: Column 3 is 55px wide, leaving 34px for text; the complete Hebrew name needs 58px. Column 5 is 188px wide, which is still too narrow for the longer notes to fit on fewer lines.

critique.good: The table fits the viewport and preserves the intact headers, codes, population figures, and words. The row heights match r2A, so the reduced notes width does not make the table taller.
critique.problems: The Hebrew name תל אביב still wraps, despite the extra space given to its column. The narrower notes column changes line breaks without improving the table’s height or the matching of the two city names.
critique.cause: Column 3 is 69px wide, leaving 48px for text—10px short of the 58px needed for the complete Hebrew name. The 14px transferred from column 5 consequently provides no visible benefit for that name.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r0A.why: City names, codes and population figures stay intact, while the notes have enough room to read comfortably. The rows remain clear despite the necessary wrapping.

r0B.why: The wider notes column reads well and population figures stay intact, but the Hebrew name for Tel Aviv wraps onto two lines.

r0C.why: The notes and population figures are easy to scan, though the Hebrew name for Tel Aviv wraps because its column is narrow.

contrast.why: The population figures break across lines, making the numbers difficult to read and compare, even though the notes have reasonable space.

ref_auto.why: Notes have a comfortable measure and population figures stay intact, but the Hebrew name for Tel Aviv wraps onto two lines.

ref_equal.why: The notes are squeezed into very narrow lines, creating tall rows and excessive whitespace elsewhere. Two population figures also split across lines.

raw.unsure: The small differences in notes-column width among B, C and E have little effect on their overall quality.

r0C.why: The population figures remain intact and the notes wrap at readable phrase lengths. The Hebrew name תל אביב splits across two lines.

ref_auto.why: The notes have a little more room and the numbers stay intact, but the Hebrew name תל אביב still wraps.

r0A.why: Both city columns and all population figures stay intact. The notes wrap naturally, and the rows remain easy to scan despite the extra line in the first row.

contrast.why: Every population figure breaks across lines, making the numbers difficult to read and compare.

ref_equal.why: The notes are squeezed into a very narrow column, producing tall, fragmented rows. Two population figures also break across lines, while other columns have ample unused space.

r0B.why: The notes are comfortably spaced and the numbers stay intact, but the Hebrew name תל אביב splits across two lines.

raw.unsure: The difference in overall quality between A, B and F is modest; each makes a similar tradeoff between space for notes and the Hebrew city name.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
